title: Nobody Knows My Order
connection_reasons: A lyric about leaving with no plan and a sparse, open loop you named 'leave this place': the same wish to be somewhere new.

next_action.action: Speak or half-sing the coffee-order lines over 'leave this place', then write two lines about arriving somewhere.

fragments.agent_narrative: This is about leaving for somewhere nobody knows you. You named a loop 'leave this place', so I put the two together.

fragments.raw_text:
leave the dishes in the sink
the dog can come obviously
I want to be somewhere
where nobody knows my coffee order
fragments.suggestion: Leaving, told through small and funny details: the dishes, the dog, the coffee order. 'Where nobody knows my coffee order' is a sharp way to say you want to be a stranger somewhere, and it could be the title line. Keep the rhythm conversational. A second verse from the other side, after arriving, would give it somewhere to go.

fragments.title: Coffee Order
leave this place
fragments.suggestion: A short, sparse loop at 123 BPM in D minor, bright in tone and with the fewest attacks in the library, about 1.3 per second. It has a sense of open space and forward lean at once, which suits a part that moves without crowding. A steady, simple pulse underneath would add motion without filling the gaps. The brightness leaves room below for a warm bass line. Try it as the opening of an arrangement, where its spaciousness can set the tone.
fragments.agent_narrative: The loop's name and its open, spacious sound match the coffee-order lyric's wish to leave. That shared wish is the link.
